title: How to Process and Search Documents with LlamaCloud and Jinba
summary: Build a RAG pipeline for enterprise PDFs and Word docs using LlamaCloud for layout-aware parsing and Jinba to wire parsing, retrieval, Azure OpenAI generation, and audit logging into one workflow.
body_markdown:
### Summary


- Extract structured data from complex PDFs, Word files, and multi-page financial reports without hand-built OCR pipelines.
- LlamaCloud parses documents with layout awareness, preserving tables, footnotes, and appendices, and stores them as queryable, embedded chunks.
- In Jinba, File Input -> LlamaCloud -> LlamaIndex retrieval -> Azure OpenAI -> automatic logs creates an auditable document Q&A pipeline with no custom connectors.
- Teams can move from months-long managed platform deployments to a same-day Jinba workflow accepting document uploads.
- Build and share the completed workflow in[Jinba Flow](https://flow.jinba.io/) so non-engineering teams can run it via a standard chat interface.


Extracting reliable, structured data from enterprise documents requires more than basic extraction. PDFs with complex tables, Word files with inconsistent layouts, and multi-page financial reports all resist the extraction approaches most pipelines start with. Teams that use OCR must bridge the gap between raw text scraping and document understanding. Those that select managed platforms often encounter implementation timelines measured in months, parse-and-index pipelines that take a full day to run, and query engines that fail without surfacing any reason why.


The combination of[LlamaCloud](https://www.llamaindex.ai/llamacloud) and[Jinba](https://jinba.io/) addresses these constraints directly. LlamaCloud handles high-fidelity document parsing and semantic retrieval. Jinba provides the workflow layer that connects parsing, retrieval, generation, and logging into a single auditable pipeline. This guide covers each step.


## What Each Tool Brings


Each component has a distinct responsibility.


LlamaCloud is a managed document automation platform built on LlamaParse. It goes beyond OCR by performing document understanding: parsing complex multi-page tables, interpreting charts, recognising layout structure, and producing chunked, embedded output that retrieval systems can query accurately. The LlamaParse engine retains context, confidence scores, and citations throughout, which makes downstream answers verifiable rather than approximate.


[Jinba](https://jinba.io/) is a platform for building, running, and deploying AI-powered workflows using natural language. It exposes LlamaCloud, Azure OpenAI, and other tools through a visual and chat-based interface called Jinba Flow, a central toolbox for registering those tools, and a Jinba App layer that enables non-engineering teams to run completed workflows through a standard chat interface. The LlamaCloud integration is handled natively: document inputs flow directly into the LlamaCloud tool without custom connector code.


Together, the two tools replace a stack that would otherwise require a parsing service, a vector store, a retrieval library, an LLM API, and a logging layer, each wired together manually.


## Step 1: Ingest Documents via File Input


Every workflow in Jinba begins with a trigger. For document processing, that trigger is a file upload handled by Jinba's[Document Processing](https://docs.jinba.io/) tool.


Supported formats include PDFs, Word documents, and other unstructured file types. Teams that previously faced months-long deployment timelines with platforms like DocuWare or M-Files can have a Jinba workflow accepting document uploads the same day.


At this stage, the goal is simple: get the file into the workflow. No preprocessing, format conversion, or manual field mapping is required. The file is passed as-is to the next step.


## Step 2: Parse and Index with LlamaCloud


Once a document is in the workflow, it is handed to the LlamaCloud tool in Jinba. This is where the extraction work happens.


LlamaParse processes the document with layout awareness. It does not treat the document as a flat string of text. Instead, it identifies structural elements: tables that span multiple pages, figures with embedded data, headers that define document sections, and blocks of text that carry different semantic weight depending on their position. The output is a set of chunks with associated embeddings, ready for retrieval.


This matters for enterprise documents specifically because the information that teams need is almost never in the easy-to-parse sections. It is in the footnotes of a financial report, the third column of a specification table, or the appendix of a contract. Parsing engines that flatten a document lose that context. LlamaParse preserves it.


The parsed and indexed content is stored in a LlamaCloud-managed index. Subsequent queries run against this index rather than the raw document, which is what makes retrieval fast and semantically accurate.


## Step 3: Retrieve and Generate with LlamaIndex and Azure OpenAI


With the index built, the workflow is ready to answer questions. This step combines two Jinba tools: the LlamaIndex retrieval layer embedded in the LlamaCloud integration, and Jinba's Azure OpenAI tool for generation.


The retrieval process works as follows:


1. A user submits a natural language query through the Jinba App interface.
2. The workflow passes the query to the LlamaIndex retrieval layer, which searches the LlamaCloud-managed index for the most relevant passages.
3. Those passages are assembled into a context block and passed to Azure OpenAI.
4. The model generates an answer grounded in the retrieved context.


The answer is bounded by what the retrieval step surfaces. The model does not speculate beyond the provided passages, which means responses are traceable back to specific sections of the source documents.


### Why Azure OpenAI for Generation


Retrieval-augmented generation introduces several constraints that the choice of LLM directly affects.[Azure AI documentation identifies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/retrieval-augmented-generation-overview) query understanding, token limits, and multi-source data access as the primary challenges in RAG pipelines. Azure OpenAI addresses all three while adding the enterprise controls that most document operations teams require: private deployment within their own Azure tenant, no data egress to shared infrastructure, and compliance alignment with organizational data governance policies.


For teams processing sensitive documents, this is not a secondary concern. The Azure OpenAI tool in Jinba connects to the organization's Azure deployment, so document content and query data remain within that environment throughout the generate step.


Semantic ranking further improves retrieval quality. Rather than returning results by keyword frequency alone, the pipeline scores passages by relevance to the intent of the query, which reduces the noise that causes LLMs to produce off-target answers.


### Where This Workflow Applies


The four-step pipeline is domain-agnostic, but a few categories of enterprise document work benefit most directly:


- **Technical documentation search:** Engineering teams querying thousands of pages of product specifications, API references, or compliance standards get precise, passage-level answers rather than a list of documents to read manually.
- **Financial due diligence:** Analysts running compliance reviews or risk assessments against financial reports, fund documents, or regulatory filings can extract specific figures and clauses without manual document review. Organizations including Cemex and Carlyle have used[LlamaParse for this type of deep research work](https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/llamacloud-one-year-later-the-complete-document-automation-platform) , reducing the time required to compile and analyze business-critical information.
- **Invoice and contract processing:** Line-item extraction from invoices, or clause identification in contracts, runs through the same parse-retrieve-generate loop. The model reads only what LlamaCloud has already structured, so the output reflects the document rather than a hallucinated approximation of it.


## Step 4: Log Every Retrieval and Generation Event


Jinba logs each step in a workflow automatically. For document search pipelines, this means the record includes:


- The file submitted at ingestion
- The query issued by the user
- The passages retrieved from the LlamaCloud index, with their source references
- The prompt sent to Azure OpenAI
- The generated response


This is not an optional add-on. The audit trail is produced by default as part of the Jinba workflow execution. Teams that need to demonstrate compliance with internal governance requirements or external regulators have a complete, time-stamped record of every retrieval and generation event without building separate logging infrastructure.


The absence of this visibility is a documented limitation in LlamaCloud deployments outside a structured orchestration layer. When a query engine produces unexpected results and there is no record of what was retrieved or how the answer was assembled, diagnosing the failure is not practical. Jinba's logging closes this gap.


## Building the Workflow in Jinba Flow


The steps above translate into a linear workflow in[Jinba Flow](https://flow.jinba.io/) :


1. **File Input node:** Accepts uploaded documents and passes them downstream.
2. **LlamaCloud node:** Receives the file, runs LlamaParse extraction, and builds or updates the index. For advanced configuration options, refer to the Jinba LlamaCloud documentation.
3. **Query node:** Accepts the user's natural language question via the Jinba App.
4. **LlamaIndex retrieval:** Runs inside the LlamaCloud integration, returning the most relevant passages from the index.
5. **Azure OpenAI node:** Receives the retrieved passages as context and generates the grounded answer.
6. **Log output:** Captured automatically at each node boundary.


Jinba Flow's visual interface handles the connections between nodes. No custom connector code is required for the LlamaCloud integration, the Azure OpenAI handoff, or the logging output. Teams that have previously needed significant engineering effort to produce reliable structured data from unstructured documents can build and test this pipeline in a single session.


## What to Watch When Deploying


A few practical considerations affect production deployments:


**Index freshness.** The LlamaCloud index reflects the documents parsed at ingestion time. When source documents are updated, the workflow needs to re-ingest them to keep the index current. Jinba workflows can be triggered on a schedule or on file upload events, so this does not require manual intervention.


**Chunk configuration.** LlamaParse's default chunking works well for most document types, but documents with very long tables or dense technical content benefit from explicit configuration. The[LlamaIndex developer documentation](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/) covers the available parameters.


**Model selection in Azure OpenAI.** The retrieved context window size affects which Azure OpenAI model is appropriate. Longer documents with denser retrieval output require models with higher token limits. This is a deployment-time configuration in the Azure OpenAI node, not a Jinba constraint.


**Sensitive document handling.** Teams processing documents that contain personally identifiable information should confirm their Azure OpenAI deployment settings align with their data residency and anonymization requirements before moving to production.


The full reference for available tools, node configurations, and workflow examples is available in the Jinba documentation.


---


LlamaCloud provides the document understanding layer that turns unstructured enterprise files into queryable, structured knowledge. Jinba provides the workflow layer that connects parsing, retrieval, generation, and logging without requiring each team to build and maintain that infrastructure themselves. The result is an intelligent document processing pipeline that is auditable by default, deployable with private models, and extensible across departments without a months-long implementation project.


Start with a single document type, validate the retrieval quality against known queries, then expand the workflow to cover additional file sources or output destinations as requirements grow.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the Jinba and LlamaCloud integration?


The Jinba and LlamaCloud integration combines LlamaCloud's document parsing and semantic retrieval with Jinba's workflow orchestration to create an end-to-end document Q&A pipeline. Jinba passes uploaded files to LlamaCloud for parsing and indexing, then uses LlamaIndex retrieval and Azure OpenAI for generation, while automatically logging every step.


### How does LlamaCloud parse complex PDFs and tables?


LlamaCloud uses layout-aware parsing through LlamaParse to identify tables, figures, headers, and multi-page structures instead of flattening documents into plain text. It preserves context such as footnotes, table columns, and appendices, then chunks and embeds the content so downstream answers remain traceable to the source.


### How do I build a document Q&A workflow with Jinba and LlamaCloud?


The workflow is built in Jinba Flow by connecting a File Input node, a LlamaCloud node, a Query node, an Azure OpenAI node, and automatic log outputs. The workflow accepts uploaded documents, parses and indexes them in LlamaCloud, retrieves relevant passages, and generates answers grounded in those passages. No custom connector code is required.


### Which document formats does the workflow support?


The workflow supports PDFs, Word documents, and other unstructured file types accepted by Jinba's Document Processing tool. Files are uploaded as-is; LlamaCloud handles format-specific layout structures without preprocessing or manual field mapping.


### Why use Azure OpenAI for retrieval-augmented generation?


Azure OpenAI addresses the main RAG challenges: query understanding, token limits, and multi-source data access, while keeping document content and queries within the organization's Azure tenant. It also enables semantic ranking, which scores retrieved passages by intent rather than keyword frequency, reducing off-target answers.


### How does Jinba log retrieval and generation events?


Jinba automatically logs the submitted file, user query, retrieved passages with source references, the prompt sent to Azure OpenAI, and the generated response. This audit trail is produced by default and helps teams diagnose retrieval failures and demonstrate compliance without building separate logging infrastructure.


### Can I use Jinba and LlamaCloud for sensitive enterprise documents?


Yes. The Azure OpenAI tool connects to the organization's private deployment, so document content and query data remain within that environment during generation. Teams processing PII should still confirm data residency and anonymization settings before production use.


### How long does it take to deploy a LlamaCloud and Jinba pipeline?


Teams can often have a Jinba workflow accepting document uploads the same day, compared with months-long timelines for some managed document platforms. The native LlamaCloud integration and visual workflow builder eliminate custom connector work, so teams can validate a single document type first and expand from there.


### What should I do when my LlamaCloud index contains outdated content?


Re-ingest the updated documents into the workflow so LlamaCloud rebuilds or updates the index. Jinba workflows can trigger on a schedule or on file upload events, keeping the index current without manual intervention.


### How does semantic retrieval improve answer accuracy?


Semantic retrieval scores passages by relevance to the intent of the query rather than keyword frequency alone. That reduces noise and allows Azure OpenAI to generate answers grounded in the most contextually relevant sections of the source documents.
